executive_summary: Apple (AAPL) grew revenue from $383.3B (FY23) to $416.2B (FY25), with growth accelerating from 2.0% (FY24) to 6.4% (FY25). Operating margin expanded each year, from 29.8% (FY23) to 31.5% (FY24) to 32.0% (FY25). Despite this improvement, Apple's FY25 margin (32.0%) trails both Microsoft (46.8% in FY26) and, more narrowly, sits above Alphabet (32.0% in FY25 — effectively tied). Microsoft shows both higher margins and faster, accelerating revenue growth (14.9% to 17.8%) than Apple. Alphabet's growth also outpaces Apple (13.9% to 15.1%) though its margin is roughly on par with Apple's. Note peers report on different fiscal calendars (MSFT: June FYE; GOOGL: Dec FYE; AAPL: Sept FYE), so year-over-year comparisons are not perfectly synchronized in calendar time.

competitive_position: Based solely on the data given, Apple's operating margin (32.0% FY25) has converged with Alphabet's (32.0% FY25) but remains well below Microsoft's (46.8% FY26). On growth, Apple (6.4% FY25) lags both Microsoft (17.8% FY26) and Alphabet (15.1% FY25) by a wide margin. Apple's margin trend is positive (three consecutive years of expansion), but so are Microsoft's and Alphabet's (with Alphabet's flattening in the most recent year). On the two metrics provided — revenue growth and operating margin — Apple is the slowest-growing of the three and no longer differentiated on margin versus Alphabet, while Microsoft leads on both dimensions.
risks: Apple's revenue growth (6.4% FY25), while improved, is less than half of Microsoft's (17.8% FY26) and Alphabet's (15.1% FY25); if this gap persists, Apple's relative market position could erode over time.

Fiscal year-end mismatches (Apple: Sept; Microsoft: June; Alphabet: Dec) mean the growth/margin figures compared here are not for identical calendar periods, which could distort like-for-like comparisons.
Alphabet's operating margin growth stalled between FY24 (32.1%) and FY25 (32.0%), which could signal margin pressure ahead for Apple's peer set generally — a dynamic not explained in the data.
No revenue growth figure is provided for Apple's FY23, Microsoft's FY24, or Alphabet's FY23, limiting the ability to assess longer-term trend consistency.
questions_for_management: What is driving the acceleration in Apple's revenue growth from 2.0% (FY24) to 6.4% (FY25), and is this expected to continue or was it a one-time factor?
Given Microsoft's operating margin (46.8% FY26) is roughly 15 points above Apple's (32.0% FY25), what structural or business-mix differences explain this gap, and does Apple see room to close it?
Alphabet's operating margin growth flattened in FY25 (32.1% to 32.0%) after strong FY24 improvement — does Apple see a similar risk of margin plateauing after three years of expansion?
